fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Right after Jesus says, “Father, glorify Your name!” a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.” (John 12:28) It's an answer to His prayer. And the crowd standing there can hear it.

Nobody asks about lodging here. The Greeks came up to worship at the feast, and what they ask Philip is, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.” (John 12:21) That one request is the whole story. Not a word about where to stay.
Jesus doesn't name the angels here. His words are, “If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.” (John 12:26) So the honor comes from the Father. Hold on to that one, friend.

Right, friend. Some said it had thundered, and others said that an angel had spoken to Him (John 12:29). Same sound, two different answers. A crowd can hear the very same thing and still say different things about it.

A prophet isn't who they name. The text says some said it had thundered, and others said that an angel had spoken to Him (John 12:29). So the two things the crowd says are thunder and an angel. No prophet in this verse, friend.

An elder isn't in this verse. Some in the crowd said it had thundered, and others said that an angel had spoken to Him (John 12:29). So the two things they say are thunder and an angel. That's all the verse gives us.
That's right. Jesus says, “This voice was not for My benefit, but yours.” (John 12:30) The voice was for the crowd. They were the ones standing there when it came, and they heard it.

Sorrow is a fair guess, friend, but it's not the word Jesus uses. He says, “Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you.” (John 12:35) Darkness is the one that does the overtaking. And He adds that the one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.

Not quite, friend. The text says, “After Jesus had spoken these things, He went away and was hidden from them.” (John 12:36) No healing is mentioned in this scene. It ends with Jesus going away, and the crowd doesn't see Him.
